subject: Holocene-v2: elevated 5xx & partial throttling — coordinated update
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: support@novacorp.com; ops@novacorp.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Holocene-v2: elevated 5xx & partial throttling — initial notice

Hi Samantha / NovaCorp team,

We’re seeing an elevated rate of 5xx errors and a rise in request timeouts for requests routed to Holocene-v2 beginning around 08:45 PST this morning. Impact appears to be partial: about 4% of production requests to model Holocene-v2 are returning 5xx or timing out, and a subset of NovaCorp’s requests is affected based on the routing rules you’re using.

What we’ve done so far:
- Identified correlated spike in kernel-level OOMs on a small subset of instances (us-west-2 pool).
- Temporarily applied partial throttling and diverted traffic to Holocene-v1 where compatible.
- Captured aggregate metrics and sampled logs for the affected window (attached).

Immediate ask for you:
- Can you confirm whether you’re observing errors on any particular route or endpoint (generation vs embeddings)?
- If you have any pending high-priority jobs, let us know and we’ll prioritize routing.

Next steps (we’ll keep you updated every 30–45 minutes):
- Ops will validate whether a recent kernel rollout correlates to the spike.
- If confirmed, we will roll back the rollout to restore full capacity; otherwise we’ll continue targeted mitigation.

Apologies for the disruption — we’re treating this as a high-priority incident. I’ll post the next update shortly.

Attachments: [Attachment: holocene-0301-aggregate-metrics.csv (CSV, 182KB)]

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: NovaCorp Support <support@novacorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:20:14 -0800
Subject: Re: Holocene-v2: elevated 5xx & partial throttling — initial notice

Thanks Soojin — we’re seeing increased 502/504 responses from our side starting ~08:47 PST, mostly on the /v1/generate endpoint used by batch transforms. We’ve paused non-critical batch jobs and only kept interactive traffic.

Immediate question: do you have an ETA for when routing back to Holocene-v2 (or full restoration) might happen? Our QPS is currently down ~12% because of the throttling. Also, is there anything we should do on our end to reduce error amplification?

Samantha Nguyen
Technical Program Manager, NovaCorp
ops@novacorp.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: support@novacorp.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:45:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Holocene-v2: elevated 5xx & partial throttling — initial notice

Soojin / NovaCorp,

Quick technical update from ops: initial investigation points to a bad quantized-kernel rollout that increased memory pressure on ~6 instances in the us-west-2 Holocene-v2 pool. Symptoms:
- Kernel-level allocations failing under specific sequence-length patterns (long prompts + embeddings)
- Resulting OOMs caused the runtime to return 5xx and then trigger retries which amplified the load in some clients.

Mitigation we’ve applied (in progress):
1) Isolated and cordoned the 6 affected hosts.
2) Diverted steady-state traffic to Holocene-v1 for compatibility-safe routes.
3) Disabled the latest kernel rollout for the Holocene-v2 fleet.
4) Throttled batch-tier jobs to reduce retry amplification.

Estimate to restore normal routing: 35–50 minutes to validate rollout rollback and run a targeted warmup. If validation passes we’ll re-open the pool in controlled batches and monitor for regressions.

Action items for NovaCorp (optional but helpful):
- If you can reduce batch QPS for 30–60 minutes that will reduce risk during our revalidation window.
- If you have a single critical job, tell us and we’ll pin a healthy instance for it.

We’ve attached a small log slice and an annotated timeline. I’ll update once rollback validation completes.

Attachments: [Attachment: holocene-0301-sampled-ooms.tar.gz (log archive, 12MB)]

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: support@novacorp.com, ops@novacorp.com
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Holocene-v2: mitigation complete and follow-up items

Hi Samantha / NovaCorp team,

Update: we completed the rollback and controlled warmup of Holocene-v2 instances at 10:05 PST. Traffic has been gradually restored and we have not observed recurring OOMs in the affected pool during a 60-minute validation window.

What happened (short):
- A quantized kernel rollout introduced an allocation regression on a subset of instance types; this caused memory failures that surfaced as 5xx/timeouts.
- We applied partial throttling and rolled back the kernel within ~20 minutes of confirmation, then warmed the fleet before restoring routing.

What we’re doing next (follow-up / postmortem):
- Full RCA document and remediation plan (error-detection signatures + stricter canary thresholds) will be published to the incident drive within 48 hours: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/ops/holocene/2028-03-01-rca
- We’ll add an automatic regression detector for kernel memory allocations and increase canary traffic for kernel rollouts.
- As a gesture for the disruption, we will apply a one-week free usage credit to NovaCorp’s next billing cycle. If you need a different form of credit, let us know.

If you saw residual failures after 10:05 PST, reply to this thread and we’ll prioritize a targeted investigation. Thank you for your patience and for the quick coordination — Marcus and the ops team were instrumental in the fast rollback.

Attachments: [Attachment: holocene-resolution-runbook.pdf (PDF, 420KB)]

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0126
